title: Perception and subliminal perception
summary: Perception is how we select, organise and interpret information. Selective attention, distortion and retention filter it; subliminal perception works below awareness.

chunks.heading: What perception is
chunks.explanation_md:
**Perception** is the process by which we **select, organize and interpret** information inputs to create a meaningful picture of the world.

A motivated person is ready to act, and how they act is influenced by their perception of the situation. In marketing, **perceptions are more important than reality** because they affect consumers' actual behavior.

Example on the slide: **packaging color affects the choice of soap** because it influences perceptions related to fragrance. The picture shows two laundry liquid bottles with the same Ultra Clean label, one orange and one white.

chunks.heading: Selective attention, distortion and retention
chunks.explanation_md:
We screen out most stimuli. Three filters:

- **Selective attention**: allocating processing capacity to some stimuli. Marketers must work hard to attract consumers' notice. People notice stimuli that relate to a **current need**, that they **anticipate**, or whose **deviations are large** compared with the normal size.
- **Selective distortion**: the tendency to interpret information in a way that fits our **preconceptions**. It can help strong brands, because consumers distort neutral or ambiguous information to be more positive, so coffee may seem to taste better, a car may drive more smoothly, and a bank wait may seem shorter, depending on the brand.
- **Selective retention**: remembering a part of the information that associates with our beliefs and forgetting what contradicts it.

chunks.heading: Subliminal perception
chunks.explanation_md:
**Subliminal perception** means perceptions developed by the **subconscious mind**, through a **visual or audio stimulus**.

The notes explain the marketing angle: some argue that marketers embed **covert, subliminal messages** in ads or packaging. Consumers are **not consciously aware** of them, yet they **affect behavior**.

So in an exam answer: define it, say the stimulus is visual or audio, say the consumer is not consciously aware, and say it can still influence behaviour.

questions.stem: Evaluate the role of subliminal perception in marketing. Explain how perception works and where subliminal perception fits.
questions.model_answer_md:
**Perception** is how we select, organize and interpret information inputs to create a meaningful picture of the world. We screen out most stimuli through **selective attention**, interpret what remains through **selective distortion** and remember part of it through **selective retention**.

**Subliminal perception** sits alongside these: perceptions developed by the **subconscious mind** from a **visual or audio stimulus**. Some argue that marketers embed covert messages in ads or packaging; consumers are **not consciously aware** of them, yet their **behavior is affected**.

**Evaluation.** The idea has long fascinated armchair marketers. Selective attention, by contrast, says marketers must work hard to attract notice.

**Conclusion.** Subliminal perception works below awareness through visual or audio stimuli and is said to affect behavior.

questions.stem: Explain selective attention, selective distortion and selective retention with examples.
questions.model_answer_md:
We screen out most stimuli, so perception works through three filters.

**Selective attention.** Allocating processing capacity to some stimulus. Marketers must work hard to attract notice. People notice stimuli that relate to a **current need**, stimuli they **anticipate**, and stimuli whose **deviations are large** compared with the normal.

**Selective distortion.** The tendency to interpret information in a way that fits **preconceptions**. It helps strong brands, because consumers distort neutral or ambiguous information to be more positive: coffee may seem to taste better, a car may drive more smoothly, and a bank wait may seem shorter, depending on the brand.

**Selective retention.** Remembering the part of information that associates with beliefs and forgetting what contradicts it.

The soap slide shows a related idea: packaging color influences perceptions related to fragrance.

**Conclusion.** The three filters mean the message a marketer sends is not the message the consumer ends up with.
